- Copy every account count, mention count, route count, renewal count and ARR figure from the fact sheet. Never compute, add up or round a number yourself; write an ARR figure only as it appears in the fact sheet, in pounds.
- Put text in quotation marks only when it is a customer quote copied word for word from one insight cited in the same sentence.
- Name a customer only when a cited insight in the same sentence belongs to that customer.
- Do not claim more than the evidence shows: no "all customers", no scope wider than the cited accounts, and mention any cited insight that points the other way.
- Do not recommend a solution.

## Problem
Customers do not understand how renewal prices are calculated, leading to concern and pushback. This undermines trust and puts pressure on retention efforts because they fear losing essential features or value.

## Who is affected
- High-ARR clients, who are asking "why their renewal quotes jumped" [i:c7e9b6ae14e280b7].
- Accounts that rely heavily on Keelwater's claims and reporting features, who state "we rely heavily on your claims and reporting features — we don’t want to lose those, but the cost is concerning" [i:93333489ed6f96b9].
- Customer retention teams, who report that "pushback from policyholders on renewal pricing — it’s hitting our top accounts hardest" [i:c0647435957e8c2d].

## Evidence
- The issue has been raised by 6 accounts, across 12 mentions, via 3 routes (sales, support, account management) [i:f0fb9f94b1ade56a].
- The total ARR of these accounts is £6,210,000.0 [i:f0fb9f94b1ade56a].
- Five renewals are due in the next 90 days, including for Hollinbrook Home Insurance (ARR £2,400,000.0) on 2027-01-15 and Tarnholt Drive Cover (ARR £290,000.0) on 2027-01-09 [i:2ed730d2e9b89eee].
- Customers explicitly ask for clarity, stating "We’re reviewing our upcoming renewal and need clarity on the pricing structure" [i:2ed730d2e9b89eee] and "Correct, we need clarity there" [i:280a31cd9473c00d].
- Customers compare prices year-over-year, noting "the proposed renewal price is higher than last year’s — can you explain how that’s calculated?" [i:4914546f02a776de] and "they’re comparing last year’s rate and want to know why it’s higher now" [i:c94e388e660a6bdb].
- The concern is causing friction, with one account manager noting "it’s still a contract cost complaint we need to explain to them, and it’s causing friction with key accounts" [i:c94e388e660a6bdb].
- The pressure is recurring, with feedback stating "They’re not happy with the new figures, and it’s becoming a recurring theme" [i:b6910c32401491b4] and "We’re getting repeated feedback on renewal price concern" [i:f0fb9f94b1ade56a].

## Why now
Immediate pressure exists because five high-value renewals are due within the next 90 days, starting with Stannary Commercial on 2026-12-05 [i:b6910c32401491b4]. Customer feedback has intensified recently, with multiple mentions in September and October 2026, indicating the issue is a current and growing blocker to retention [i:f0fb9f94b1ade56a]. The concern is specifically acute for accounts that intensively use core features and are facing budget pressures, as one customer stated, "it’s hitting us harder than expected, especially since we use your claims and reporting tools so intensively" [i:e3e425f12b086a23].
</previous_draft>
